# Transformation Router Prompt System Implemented

Created transformation-router.ts with AI classification, keyword-based analysis, fallback quick-classify, and refinement capabilities totaling 421 lines

The transformation-router.ts file implements the critical entry point for the P2-05 transformation agent system, providing both AI-powered and keyword-based classification capabilities to automatically detect transformation types and route conversations to appropriate expert personas. This 421-line implementation represents the first completed component of the 6-task P2-05c sequence.

The system prompt establishes the AI as a transformation project analysis expert with clear classification criteria for four transformation types. TECHNICAL transformations (🔧) focus on architecture, performance, APIs, infrastructure, and security with indicators like performance/latency mentions, security/RGPD/CI-CD/tests keywords, and SLO/SLA/scalability/technical debt focus. ORGANIZATIONAL transformations (🏢) center on culture, process, change management, and HR with indicators including teams/culture/management mentions, process/governance/roles keywords, and time-to-market/eNPS/adoption focus. BUSINESS transformations (💼) target customer value, market positioning, and commercial strategy with indicators like client/market/value mentions, competition/product/GTM keywords, and acquisition/retention/satisfaction focus. HYBRID transformations (🔀) represent significant combinations of at least two domains with clear interdependencies requiring multi-dimensional approaches.

The keyword dictionaries provide comprehensive domain signal detection with 80+ carefully selected French terms. TECHNICAL_KEYWORDS (46 terms) covers performance/architecture (performance, latence, scalabilité, microservices, API, REST, GraphQL), infrastructure (cloud, AWS/GCP/Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, database, SQL/NoSQL), development (code, CI/CD, pipeline, tests, coverage, dette technique, refactoring, migration), security/compliance (sécurité, RGPD, OAuth, chiffrement, TLS, audit, PCI-DSS), and technical metrics (SLO, SLA, uptime, MTTR, MTBF, TPS). ORGANIZATIONAL_KEYWORDS (39 terms) spans culture/people (culture, équipe, management, RH, compétences), change management (changement, adoption, résistance, formation, onboarding), governance/process (processus, gouvernance, rôles, workflow, méthodologie, agile), stakeholders (parties prenantes, sponsor, CSE, syndicats, ambassadeurs), and organizational metrics (eNPS, engagement, time-to-market, silos, transversalité). BUSINESS_KEYWORDS (45 terms) encompasses customer/market (client, utilisateur, marché, segment, persona, B2B/B2C), value/product (valeur, proposition de valeur, produit, MVP, feature, UX), competition/strategy (concurrence, différenciation, positionnement, GTM, commercialisation), financial/metrics (revenus, CA, coûts, ROI, conversion, acquisition, rétention, churn, NPS), and business process (parcours client, customer journey, funnel, panier, vente).

The analysis pipeline combines keyword matching with intelligent scoring. analyzeTransformationSignals normalizes input text to lowercase, filters each keyword dictionary for matches, calculates domain scores as matched signal count divided by total signals across all domains, and defaults to equal 0.33 scores if zero signals detected preventing division by zero. determineTransformationType implements sophisticated HYBRID detection logic sorting the three domain scores descending, comparing top scorer against second scorer, identifying HYBRID scenario when score difference is less than 0.15 (close competition) or when top score is below 0.5 while second exceeds 0.25 (no clear winner), setting HYBRID confidence as sum of top two scores capped at 0.9, otherwise returning the winning type with its score as confidence and corresponding persona suggestion (tech/orga/metier).

The prompt generation layer provides flexible classification requests. buildRouterPrompt constructs multi-section prompts with user description in quotes, optional additional context section, signal analysis instruction, and explicit JSON format specification defining all expected fields including type enum, confidence float, reasoning explanation (2-3 sentences), suggestedPersona enum, detectedSignals object with per-domain arrays, and primaryFocus summary sentence. buildRouterRefinementPrompt enables dynamic reclassification after conversation reveals new context, presenting initial type and conversation summary, asking whether new elements warrant reclassification, and requesting shouldReclassify boolean with optional newType and reasoning, supporting adaptive classification that improves as more context emerges.

Response parsing implements robust extraction with validation and fallbacks. parseRouterResponse uses regex /\{[\s\S]*"type"[\s\S]*\}/ to locate JSON in potentially text-wrapped responses, validates type field against TECHNICAL/ORGANIZATIONAL/BUSINESS/HYBRID values returning null for invalid types, validates suggestedPersona against tech/orga/metier defaulting to 'tech' for invalid values, clamps confidence to 0-1 range with 0.5 default for missing/invalid values, and uses reasoning field with primaryFocus fallback for explanation text. parseRefinementResponse similarly extracts and validates shouldReclassify boolean with optional newType and reasoning, enabling conversation-driven classification refinement.

The quickClassify function provides critical AI-free fallback enabling instant classification without API calls. This function chains analyzeTransformationSignals for keyword detection with determineTransformationType for scoring and type selection, builds reasoning from top 5 detected signals formatted as "tech:keyword, orga:keyword, métier:keyword", and returns complete RouterResult with type/confidence/reasoning/suggestedPersona. This fallback serves dual purposes: immediate classification when AI unavailable due to network/quota/error conditions, and pre-analysis feeding into AI prompt to guide Gemini's classification leveraging both keyword heuristics and semantic understanding.

Helper functions enhance UI integration. getTransformationEmoji maps types to visual indicators (TECHNICAL→🔧, ORGANIZATIONAL→🏢, BUSINESS→💼, HYBRID→🔀) with 📋 fallback, while getPersonaLabel provides French display names (tech→"Expert Technique", orga→"Expert Conduite du Changement", metier→"Expert Métier/Produit") for user-facing persona identification.

This implementation completes task #1 of the P2-05c sequence, establishing the foundational routing logic that determines which specialized persona (tech, orga, or metier) will conduct the subsequent transformation conversation. The router's dual-mode operation (AI-powered + keyword-based fallback) ensures reliable classification under all conditions while the refinement capability enables adaptive classification as conversations reveal additional context.

Business variables track NPS deltas (customer satisfaction: T0=30, Target=40), revenue growth percentages (additional revenue: T0=0%, Target=+5%), conversion rate improvements (conversion: T0=2%, Target=5%), and support cost reductions (support costs: T0=baseline, Target=-15%).

# ESLint Warnings in Export Dialog Component

Two react-hooks warnings found about React Hook Form watch function memoization in export-dialog.tsx

The lint check revealed two warnings in src/components/export/export-dialog.tsx related to React Hook Form usage. Both warnings occur where the code calls form.watch() to access form field values - one for 'format' (line 211) and one for 'unit' (line 216). ESLint's react-hooks/incompatible-library rule identifies that React Hook Form's watch() function returns a value that cannot be safely memoized, which could lead to performance or stale data issues. While these are warnings rather than errors (allowing the build to pass), they indicate a code smell where the component may not be optimally handling form state. The typical fix would be to use watch as a hook at the component level (const format = watch('format')) rather than calling it inline (watch('format')). These warnings may have been introduced in recent modifications to export-dialog.tsx (which shows as modified in git status). The presence of warnings suggests the code is functional but could be optimized following React Hook Form best practices.

# Prisma Schema with Complete Transformation Models for P2-05

Schema includes 12 models with 4 transformation tables supporting sessions, fields, variables with T0/Target/Current values, and message history

The Prisma schema provides the complete database foundation for P2-05d service implementation with four transformation-specific models integrated into the existing OKR platform schema. The schema follows PostgreSQL as the datasource and generates the Prisma JavaScript client for type-safe database access. The core OKR models (Organization, Team, User, TeamMember, Objective, KeyResult, Initiative, CheckIn, Comment) establish the foundational platform structure with proper relations and cascade behaviors. The transformation system extends this foundation with four specialized models implementing the architecture defined in P2-05a. TransformationSession serves as the root entity capturing session metadata including userId and orgId for multi-tenant isolation, title for user identification, type enum storing TECHNICAL/ORGANIZATIONAL/BUSINESS/HYBRID classification, status tracking progression through draft/in_progress/completed/archived states, and standard timestamps. Relations connect sessions to User, Organization, and the three dependent models (fields, variables, messages) with indexes on userId, orgId, and status enabling efficient list queries filtered by user, organization, or completion state. TransformationField implements the axis-based data collection with sessionId foreign key, axis string storing the specific transformation axis name, value as Text type supporting large textual responses, metadata JSON for structured additional data, and a unique constraint on [sessionId, axis] ensuring each axis is collected exactly once per session with proper index on sessionId for retrieval. TransformationVariable realizes the T0-Target-Current measurement pattern central to the INIT1 model with sessionId relation, name and description identifying the metric, category for classification (performance/quality/adoption/risk/financial/operational/satisfaction/efficiency), valueT0 capturing the baseline measurement, valueTarget storing the objective goal, valueCurrent defaulting to 0 and updated via P2-06 document analysis, unit for display formatting, and optional keyResultId establishing the critical link to the OKR system enabling transformation variables to drive KeyResult progression. The unique constraint [sessionId, name] prevents duplicate variables within a session while the keyResultId foreign key without cascade allows variables to outlive their linked KeyResults. TransformationMessage provides conversation persistence with sessionId relation, role enum (user/assistant/system), content as Text for potentially long messages, metadata JSON capturing persona used and axes covered enabling conversation reconstruction, createdAt timestamp for chronological ordering, and indexes on both sessionId for session retrieval and createdAt for time-based queries. The cascade delete strategy ensures data integrity: Organization deletion cascades to TransformationSession (multi-tenant cleanup), and TransformationSession deletion cascades to fields, variables, and messages (complete session removal). This schema design supports the P2-05d service requirements for CRUD operations on sessions with field management by axis, variable tracking with T0/Target/Current values, message history persistence, and OKR integration through the keyResultId link on TransformationVariable.

# Complete Transformation TypeScript Types System with 858 Lines

Types file provides 4 enums with const assertion, 40 axis definitions with metadata arrays, base and extended interfaces, 13 DTOs, and 8 utility functions

The transformation.ts types file provides comprehensive TypeScript type definitions spanning 858 lines to support the entire transformation feature with complete type safety from database through API to UI. The enum layer uses const assertion patterns enabling both compile-time type checking and runtime value access across TransformationType (TECHNICAL/ORGANIZATIONAL/BUSINESS/HYBRID), TransformationSessionStatus (draft/in_progress/completed/archived), ChatRole (user/assistant/system), and VariableCategory with 8 metric classifications (performance/quality/adoption/risk/financial/operational/satisfaction/efficiency). The axis definitions extend beyond simple enums to provide rich metadata for all 40 transformation axes extracted from FORMULAIRES - Orchestration.txt. TECHNICAL_AXES_METADATA defines 12 axes including problematique (define performance gap), objectifs_kpi (translate business to SLO/SLA), personas_volumes (quantify system load), fonctionnalites_mvp (list architecture blocks), contraintes_techniques (detail architecture/tech choices), contraintes_organisationnelles (team processes), non_objectifs (exclusions), donnees_existantes (document data schemas), conformite_risque (compliance mechanisms), questions_ouvertes (architecture decisions), planning_jalonne (link milestones to deliverables), and indicateurs_succes (technical Definition of Done). ORGANIZATIONAL_AXES_METADATA covers 14 axes for change management including perimetre_organisationnel (entities/processes/sites), parties_prenantes (key actors/sponsors), culture_maturite (management style/readiness), impacts_humains (role/skill changes), processus_cibles (future governance), contraintes_regulation (legal obligations), risques_majeurs (social/image/continuity risks), and conduite_changement (communication/training actions). BUSINESS_AXES_METADATA defines 14 business-focused axes including cible_client (customer persona), proposition_valeur (unique promise to deliver), contexte_concurrentiel (alternative solutions), impacts_operationnels (role/task changes), parcours_client (future customer flow), contraintes_commerciales (market obligations), risques_metier (threats to value/brand/relationships), and strategie_gtm (go-to-market actions). Each axis includes human-readable label in French, detailed description explaining collection purpose, required boolean indicating if mandatory for completion, and order number enabling sequential UI presentation. The getAxesMetadataByType function intelligently handles all four transformation types with special HYBRID logic that merges unique axes from all three types using Map-based deduplication on axis keys, then sorts by order number ensuring consistent presentation. Base interfaces exactly mirror the Prisma schema with proper nullable types and typed metadata objects rather than generic JSON: TransformationSession captures user/org IDs, title, type enum, status enum, and timestamps; TransformationField stores axis-value pairs with TransformationFieldMetadata supporting completedAt timestamp, confidence scoring, and extractedVariables array; TransformationVariable implements the T0-Target-Current measurement pattern with name, description, category enum, valueT0 baseline, valueTarget objective, valueCurrent tracking defaulting to 0, unit string, and optional keyResultId linking to OKR system; TransformationMessage maintains conversation history with role enum, content text, and TransformationMessageMetadata capturing persona used, axesCovered array, variablesExtracted array, and confidence scoring. Extended interfaces compose relations through inheritance supporting various query patterns: TransformationSessionWithFields for field includes, TransformationSessionWithVariables for variable includes, TransformationSessionWithMessages for message history, TransformationSessionFull for complete session data with all relations, and TransformationVariableWithKeyResult for variables joined with their linked KeyResult data. The API DTO layer separates concerns with distinct Create/Update input types and structured response types: CreateTransformationSessionInput accepts title, type, and optional initialDescription; CreateTransformationFieldInput specifies sessionId, axis, value, and optional metadata; CreateTransformationVariableInput defines sessionId, name, valueT0, valueTarget with optional description/category/unit; CreateTransformationMessageInput provides sessionId, role, content, and optional metadata; Update inputs use Partial patterns allowing selective field updates; Response types include TransformationSessionResponse bundling session with progress, TransformationProgress tracking axis/variable completion metrics, and TransformationSessionListItem for list views. Chat API types support the conversational interface: ChatRequest contains sessionId and message; ChatResponse bundles message with optional detectedType, axesCovered, variablesExtracted, suggestedNextAxis, and sessionProgress; ChatStreamEvent enables server-sent events with type discriminator (text/metadata/variable/complete/error) and corresponding content. Advanced types support AI workflow: RouterResult captures type detection with confidence/reasoning/suggestedPersona; PersonaContext maintains conversation state with sessionType, completed/pending axes, currentAxis, extractedVariables, and conversationHistory; ExtractedVariableRaw represents AI-extracted metrics with confidence and sourceText before persistence; VariableExtractionResult bundles variables with axisCompleted flag and suggestedNextQuestions. Type guards enable runtime validation: isTransformationType, isTransformationSessionStatus, isChatRole, and isVariableCategory validate unknown values against enum options. Utility functions provide business logic: calculateSessionProgress computes completion percentage from required axes only; getNextPendingAxis returns first pending required axis ordered by sequence; canCompleteSession validates readiness returning canComplete boolean with missingAxes array and missingVariables flag; format functions translate internal enum values to French display labels for UI consumption. This comprehensive type system ensures complete type safety and enables IntelliSense/autocomplete throughout the transformation feature implementation.

# Objective Service Reference Implementation Pattern

Service layer with 340 lines demonstrates CRUD operations, relations handling, filtering, pagination, and progress calculations using Prisma client

The objective.service.ts file serves as a reference implementation demonstrating service layer patterns for P2-05d transformation service development. The 340-line service organizes 21 functions into four logical sections with clear separation of concerns. READ operations provide various retrieval patterns starting with getObjectiveById for basic entity fetch using Prisma's findUnique with simple where clause, getObjectiveWithKeyResults demonstrating Prisma's include pattern for one-level relation loading, and getObjectiveWithRelations showing deep nested includes loading owner/team/parent/children plus keyResults with their checkIns (ordered desc, take 5) and initiatives, followed by post-query processing to map keyResults adding calculated progress property using the internal calculateKeyResultProgressFromValues helper. The getObjectives function implements comprehensive filtering and pagination with ObjectiveFiltersInput supporting multiple filter dimensions: status as single value or array using { in: filters.status } pattern, period string match, teamId/ownerId/parentId foreign key filters, and search string using OR clause across title/description with case-insensitive contains mode. The where clause construction uses conditional spread operators checking for undefined to exclude filters not provided. Pagination follows standard pattern with page defaulting to 1, limit defaulting to 20, skip calculation as (page - 1) * limit, Promise.all executing parallel queries for data and count, and returning PaginatedResponse with data array plus meta object containing page/limit/total/totalPages/hasMore for client-side pagination controls. Specialized read functions getRootObjectives, getChildObjectives, getObjectivesByTeam, getObjectivesByOwner demonstrate filtered queries using where conditions with parentId null for roots, specific parentId for children, teamId for team objectives, ownerId for user objectives, all with optional period filtering and consistent orderBy createdAt desc. WRITE operations follow clean patterns: createObjective accepts CreateObjectiveInput, uses Prisma create with explicit field mapping, defaults status to 'draft' if not provided, returns typed Objective; updateObjective accepts UpdateObjectiveInput, uses conditional spreads checking !== undefined to handle partial updates including explicit null values, uses Prisma update with where id clause; deleteObjective simply calls Prisma delete with where id. PROGRESS operations demonstrate business logic integration: getObjectiveProgress fetches objective with keyResults include, maps keyResults to data objects with required fields, delegates to getObjectiveProgressSummary utility from okr-calculations passing id, keyResultsData array, and endDate; updateObjectiveStatus provides dedicated status update operation separate from general update. UTILITY operations support common queries: objectiveExists checks count > 0 pattern, hasKeyResults counts related keyResults, getDistinctPeriods uses Prisma distinct with select limiting returned fields for performance. The service consistently uses type assertions casting Prisma results to domain types imported from @/types/okr, imports Prisma singleton from @/lib/db, imports validation schemas from @/lib/validations/okr, and imports utility functions from @/lib/utils/okr-calculations. This pattern establishes conventions for P2-05d: organize functions by operation type (READ/WRITE/PROGRESS/UTILITY), use conditional spreads for flexible filtering and updates, implement pagination with parallel data/count queries, delegate calculations to utility functions, use type assertions for Prisma result typing, provide both simple and relation-loaded retrieval functions, and separate specialized updates (like status) from general updates.

# API Routes Structure Pattern with Two Route Files

Glob reveals Next.js API route organization with collection route at root level and individual resource route using dynamic id parameter

The glob search reveals the API route structure pattern for objectives that should be replicated for transformation sessions in P2-05d. Next.js App Router uses file-system based routing where route.ts files define HTTP handlers for their directory path. The objectives API implements standard RESTful organization with two files: route.ts at the collection level (src/app/api/objectives/route.ts) handling GET for listing objectives with filtering/pagination and POST for creating new objectives, and route.ts within the [id] dynamic segment directory (src/app/api/objectives/[id]/route.ts) handling GET for retrieving a specific objective, PUT for updates, and DELETE for removal. The [id] directory name using square brackets signals a dynamic route parameter that Next.js extracts from the URL and passes to route handlers, enabling pattern matching like /api/objectives/abc-123 where "abc-123" becomes the id parameter. This two-file pattern provides clean separation between collection operations (list, create) and resource operations (get, update, delete) following HTTP verb semantics and RESTful conventions. For P2-05d implementation, the transformation sessions API should follow this exact structure: src/app/api/transformation-sessions/route.ts for GET (list sessions with filters like userId, orgId, status, type) and POST (create new session with title and type), plus src/app/api/transformation-sessions/[id]/route.ts for GET (retrieve specific session with optional includes for fields/variables/messages), PUT (update session title, type, or status), and DELETE (remove session cascading to related records). Additional nested routes may be needed for sub-resources like /api/transformation-sessions/[id]/fields, /api/transformation-sessions/[id]/variables, and /api/transformation-sessions/[id]/messages if granular CRUD operations are required beyond including them in the main session GET response.

# API Collection Route Pattern with Auth, Validation, and Error Handling

Reference implementation shows Supabase auth, Zod validation, query parameter parsing, pagination, and comprehensive error handling with status codes

The objectives collection route provides a comprehensive reference pattern for implementing the transformation-sessions API route in task 2. The 154-line file implements two HTTP handlers following Next.js App Router conventions with named async function exports. Both handlers begin with identical authentication flows using createClient() from Supabase server utilities to create a server-side client, calling auth.getUser() to retrieve the authenticated user, checking for authError or null user conditions, and immediately returning NextResponse.json with 401 status and structured error object containing error message and code field for client-side handling. The GET handler demonstrates sophisticated query parameter handling starting with new URL(request.url) to access searchParams, extracting filter parameters (status, period, teamId, ownerId, parentId, search) with || undefined fallback converting empty strings to undefined for clean conditional logic, extracting pagination parameters (page defaulting to '1', limit defaulting to '20') as strings for Zod parsing, validating both using objectiveFiltersSchema.parse() and paginationSchema.parse() which throw ZodError on invalid inputs caught by the outer try-catch. The orgId requirement demonstrates parameter validation with searchParams.get('orgId') followed by null check returning 400 status with descriptive error message and MISSING_ORG_ID code. Service layer invocation passes three arguments (orgId, filters, pagination) to getObjectives which returns PaginatedResponse, then calls getDistinctPeriods(orgId) for filter metadata, spreading service result into response and augmenting with filters object containing periods array providing clients with available filter options. The POST handler shows body parsing with await request.json(), validation via createObjectiveSchema.parse(body) throwing ZodError on invalid structure/types, service invocation with createObjective(validatedData), and 201 Created status response with created entity JSON. Error handling implements three-tier hierarchy: ZodError caught first returning 400 Bad Request with structured response containing error message, VALIDATION_ERROR code, and details array exposing Zod's issues for client-side field-level error display; authentication errors returning 401 Unauthorized; generic errors falling through to console.error logging with 500 Internal Server Error and INTERNAL_ERROR code. This pattern establishes conventions for P2-05d: authenticate first and early return on failure, parse query params with undefined fallbacks, validate inputs with Zod schemas, check required parameters explicitly, call service layer with validated data, return structured error responses with message/code/details fields, use appropriate HTTP status codes (200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 500 Internal Server Error), and include metadata in responses (like periods for filters) to support rich client UIs.

# Transformation Validation Schemas Implemented with 198 Lines

Comprehensive Zod schemas created for transformation domain covering sessions, fields, variables, messages, filters, and chat requests with 9 type exports

The transformation validation schemas file has been created as a foundational component for P2-05d, establishing type-safe request validation for the transformation feature. The 198-line implementation follows the established patterns from src/lib/validations/okr.ts while adapting to transformation-specific domain requirements. The file begins with enum schema definitions importing const enums from @/types/transformation to ensure consistency between runtime validation and compile-time types. The transformationTypeSchema validates the four transformation types (TECHNICAL, ORGANIZATIONAL, BUSINESS, HYBRID), transformationSessionStatusSchema covers the four session states (draft, in_progress, completed, archived), chatRoleSchema validates the three conversation roles (user, assistant, system), and variableCategorySchema encompasses all eight metric categories (performance, quality, adoption, risk, financial, operational, satisfaction, efficiency). The common schemas section defines uuidSchema with French error message 'ID invalide' for consistent ID validation across all transformation entities. Session schemas separate create and update concerns with createTransformationSessionSchema requiring three core fields (title with 3-200 character constraint matching UI input limits, type enum from transformationTypeSchema, optional initialDescription capped at 2000 characters for user's initial context description that feeds the AI router) while updateTransformationSessionSchema uses .optional() on all fields enabling partial updates with title/type/status modifications without requiring complete object replacement. Field schemas support axis-based data collection with createTransformationFieldSchema requiring sessionId for relationship establishment, axis string constrained to 1-100 characters (matching axis keys from TECHNICAL_AXES_METADATA/ORGANIZATIONAL_AXES_METADATA/BUSINESS_AXES_METADATA), value string with minimum length ensuring non-empty responses, and optional metadata JSON for extensible structured data storage, while updateTransformationFieldSchema provides partial update capability for value and metadata refinement as conversation progresses. Variable schemas implement the T0-Target-Current measurement pattern with createTransformationVariableSchema requiring sessionId linking to parent session, name constrained to 2-100 characters for metric identification, valueT0 and valueTarget as required numbers establishing baseline and objective, optional description for human-readable explanation, optional category from variableCategorySchema for classification, and optional unit string for display formatting (%, points, days, etc.), while updateTransformationVariableSchema enables all fields as optional with nullable() supporting explicit null assignment for description/category/unit/keyResultId, including valueCurrent for P2-06 document analysis updates and keyResultId for OKR integration linking variables to KeyResult entities. Message schema supports conversation persistence with createTransformationMessageSchema requiring sessionId, role from chatRoleSchema (user/assistant/system), content string with generous 10000 character limit accommodating lengthy AI responses, and optional metadata JSON capturing persona used, axes covered, variables extracted, and confidence scores for conversation reconstruction and analysis. Filter schemas enable rich query interfaces with transformationSessionFiltersSchema using z.union() pattern allowing status as single transformationSessionStatusSchema or array enabling multi-status filtering like ['draft', 'in_progress'], type as single or array supporting queries across multiple transformation types, and optional search string for text-based filtering across titles and descriptions. The paginationSchema reuses the standard pattern with z.coerce.number() converting string query parameters, int/positive validators, max(100) limit cap, and defaults (page: 1, limit: 20) simplifying client integration. The chatRequestSchema prepares for P2-05e chat API with sessionId linking message to session context and message string constrained to 5000 characters for user input with reasonable conversation limits. Type exports use z.infer extracting TypeScript types from runtime schemas ensuring schemas serve as single source of truth where validation rules automatically propagate to type definitions used throughout service layer and API routes, matching the domain interfaces already defined in src/types/transformation.ts while adding validation constraints. This file completes the validation foundation enabling type-safe, validated inputs for the transformation-session.service.ts (task 1), /api/transformation-sessions routes (tasks 2-3), and future chat API (task P2-05e).

# Transformation Session Service Implemented with 695 Lines and 47 Functions

Complete CRUD service created covering sessions, fields, variables, and messages with read/write operations, progress tracking, unique constraints, and utility functions

The transformation-session.service.ts file has been implemented as the core business logic layer for P2-05d, providing 47 functions across 695 lines organized into 10 logical sections mirroring the patterns established in objective.service.ts. The implementation handles four entity types (sessions, fields, variables, messages) with comprehensive CRUD operations plus specialized functions for progress tracking, ownership validation, and OKR integration. Session operations provide multiple retrieval patterns with getTransformationSessionById for basic fetch, getTransformationSessionWithFields/WithVariables/WithMessages for selective relation loading, and getTransformationSessionFull for complete session data with all three relation types included using nested orderBy clauses ensuring chronological ordering. The getTransformationSessions function implements sophisticated filtering supporting orgId for multi-tenant isolation, optional userId for user-specific queries, status filter accepting single value or array using { in: filters.status } pattern, type filter similarly supporting single or array, and search string with case-insensitive contains on title field. Pagination follows standard pattern with page/limit defaults (1/20), skip calculation, Promise.all executing parallel queries for session data and total count, post-query mapping calculating progress for each session by extracting completedAxes from included fields and calling calculateSessionProgress utility function imported from @/types/transformation, returning PaginatedResponse with data array and comprehensive meta object. Session write operations include createTransformationSession accepting CreateTransformationSessionInput plus userId/orgId parameters auto-populated from authentication context, defaulting status to 'draft', updateTransformationSession using conditional spreads enabling partial updates of title/type/status, deleteTransformationSession with simple delete cascading to related entities via Prisma schema configuration, and specialized updateTransformationSessionStatus for isolated status changes. The getTransformationSessionProgress function demonstrates business logic integration fetching session with limited field/variable selects, calling getAxesMetadataByType to determine total axes for the transformation type, calculating completedAxes count, invoking calculateSessionProgress for percentage, counting variables with linked KeyResults, returning comprehensive TransformationProgress object. Field operations handle axis-based data collection with getTransformationFieldByAxis leveraging the unique sessionId_axis compound index defined in Prisma schema enabling efficient lookups, createTransformationField with metadata defaulting to empty object, updateTransformationField with conditional spreads, and innovative upsertTransformationField using Prisma's upsert operation with sessionId_axis constraint enabling idempotent field updates where repeated calls with same session/axis update existing field rather than creating duplicates or throwing errors. Variable operations implement the T0-Target-Current measurement pattern with createTransformationVariable initializing valueCurrent to valueT0 establishing baseline before P2-06 document analysis updates, getTransformationVariableByName using sessionId_name unique constraint for lookups, updateTransformationVariable supporting all eight updatable fields with conditional spreads, and specialized linkVariableToKeyResult/unlinkVariableFromKeyResult functions encapsulating the OKR integration logic enabling transformation variables to drive KeyResult progression. Message operations support conversation persistence with getTransformationMessagesBySession accepting optional limit parameter, getRecentTransformationMessages using desc ordering then reversing results to return chronological messages (most recent last) suitable for chat UI display, createTransformationMessage with metadata defaulting to empty object, and deleteTransformationMessagesBySession using deleteMany for bulk conversation clearing. Utility operations provide essential helpers with transformationSessionExists using count pattern, isTransformationSessionOwner performing permission check by comparing session.userId with provided userId enabling authorization logic in API routes, countTransformationSessionsByOrg/ByUser for dashboard statistics, and getCompletedAxes extracting axis strings from fields enabling external progress calculations. The service consistently imports prisma singleton from @/lib/db, imports domain types from @/types/transformation, imports validation input types from @/lib/validations/transformation, uses type assertions casting Prisma results to domain interfaces, employs conditional spreads with !== undefined checks supporting partial updates including explicit null values, includes orderBy clauses on relations ensuring predictable ordering, and delegates calculation logic to utility functions (calculateSessionProgress, getAxesMetadataByType) promoting separation of concerns. This implementation completes task 1 providing the foundational service layer that tasks 2-3 API routes will consume, establishing patterns for fields/variables/messages CRUD that P2-05e chat API will leverage, and enabling progress tracking and OKR integration that P2-05g pages will utilize.

Variable schema tests provide 8 comprehensive cases validating createTransformationVariableSchema requires sessionId UUID, name (2-100 chars), valueT0 baseline number, valueTarget objective number, supports optional description/category/unit fields, rejects single-character names, iterates all 8 VariableCategory values (performance/quality/adoption/risk/financial/operational/satisfaction/efficiency) confirming category enum exhaustiveness, and validates updateTransformationVariableSchema supports valueCurrent updates for P2-06 document analysis, keyResultId linking with UUID, and explicit null for unlinking enabling OKR integration toggle. Technical transformations use 12 axes covering problem definition, KPIs, personas/volumes, MVP features, technical constraints, organizational constraints, non-objectives, existing data, compliance/risk, open questions, milestone planning, and success indicators. Organizational and business transformations each define 14 axes tailored to their domains, with organizational focusing on change management dimensions (stakeholders, culture/maturity, human impacts, target processes, change management plans) and business emphasizing market aspects (client targets, value propositions, competitive context, customer journeys, GTM strategies). Each axis includes AxisMetadata with key, label, description, required flag, and order number enabling progressive conversation flows. The metadata arrays (TECHNICAL_AXES_METADATA, ORGANIZATIONAL_AXES_METADATA, BUSINESS_AXES_METADATA) provide complete context for AI personas to generate appropriate questions. # AI Suggestions API Route with Rate Limiting and Type-Safe Validation

POST endpoint handling three suggestion types with Zod validation, in-memory rate limiting at 10 requests per minute, and structured error handling

The AI suggestions API route at src/app/api/ai/suggest/route.ts provides a production-ready endpoint for OKR improvement suggestions powered by Google Gemini. The route implements a POST handler supporting three distinct suggestion workflows: improving objective formulations, generating key result suggestions for objectives, and enhancing individual key result definitions. Request validation uses Zod schemas ensuring type safety with ObjectiveContextSchema validating title, description, period, optional teamName, and optional existingKeyResults array, and KeyResultContextSchema validating objective context plus metric details including start/target/current values. In-memory rate limiting protects the API with a simple but effective Map-based implementation tracking request counts per IP address with 60-second sliding windows enforcing a maximum of 10 requests per minute, returning 429 status when exceeded. The handler first checks Gemini client availability via isGeminiAvailable, immediately returning 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE if the GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY environment variable is missing, preventing cryptic errors downstream. After rate limit and availability checks, the route validates incoming JSON against the SuggestionRequestSchema which unions ObjectiveContext and KeyResultContext, returning detailed validation errors via Zod's flatten method when validation fails. Request routing logic switches on suggestion type selecting appropriate system prompts and prompt builders: improve_objective uses SYSTEM_PROMPT_OBJECTIVE_IMPROVEMENT with buildObjectiveImprovementPrompt, suggest_key_results uses SYSTEM_PROMPT_KEY_RESULTS_GENERATION with buildKeyResultsSuggestionPrompt and enables JSON parsing, and improve_key_result uses SYSTEM_PROMPT_OBJECTIVE_IMPROVEMENT with buildKeyResultImprovementPrompt. The generateContent call configures the Gemini API with maxOutputTokens set to 1500 allowing detailed responses and temperature of 0.7 balancing creativity with coherence. Response parsing applies specifically to suggest_key_results requests where parseKeyResultsSuggestion attempts to extract structured JSON from Gemini's response, returning both parsed suggestions and raw text if parsing succeeds, or falling back to plain text response. Comprehensive error handling catches and categorizes failures: quota/rate errors return 429 RATE_LIMITED, API key errors return 500 API_ERROR, generic errors return 500 with French error messages. A complementary GET handler enables health checks returning service availability status and model identifier. This implementation provides the API pattern that P2-05e streaming chat route can adapt, particularly the rate limiting, availability checking, Zod validation, and structured error handling approaches.

The transformation-router.ts module implements a sophisticated two-tier classification system determining whether user-described transformations are TECHNICAL, ORGANIZATIONAL, BUSINESS, or HYBRID in nature. The system combines rapid keyword-based analysis with optional AI-powered deep classification using Google Gemini. Three comprehensive keyword dictionaries define domain vocabularies: TECHNICAL_KEYWORDS captures infrastructure and development terms like performance, latence, architecture, microservices, cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure), kubernetes, docker, database technologies, code development concepts (CI/CD, tests, coverage, dette technique, refactoring), security terms (sécurité, RGPD, OAuth, authentification, chiffrement), and technical metrics (SLO, SLA, uptime, MTTR, MTBF, TPS, QPS); ORGANIZATIONAL_KEYWORDS encompasses people and process terms including culture, équipe, management, collaborateurs, RH, change management vocabulary (changement, adoption, résistance, accompagnement, formation), governance concepts (processus, gouvernance, rôles, workflow, méthodologie, agile), stakeholder references (parties prenantes, sponsor, comité, CSE, syndicats), and organizational metrics (eNPS, engagement, time-to-market, productivité, silos, transversalité); BUSINESS_KEYWORDS covers market and customer language including client terminology, market segments, personas, value propositions, product/service terms, competitive landscape (concurrence, différenciation, positionnement, stratégie, GTM), financial metrics (revenus, CA, coûts, marge, ROI, conversion, acquisition, rétention, churn, LTV, CAC), satisfaction indicators (NPS, fidélisation), and customer journey concepts (parcours client, tunnel, funnel, panier). The analyzeTransformationSignals function performs case-insensitive keyword matching against input text, calculating weighted scores for each domain by counting matched keywords and returning both scores and the actual matched terms for transparency. The determineTransformationType function interprets these scores sorting domains by relevance and detecting HYBRID scenarios when the top two scores differ by less than 0.15 or when multiple domains show significant representation (top under 0.5 with second over 0.25), ensuring complex multi-domain transformations are correctly identified. The buildRouterPrompt function generates structured prompts for AI validation requesting JSON responses containing type classification, confidence score from 0 to 1, reasoning in 2-3 sentences, suggested persona (tech/orga/metier), detected signals organized by domain, and primary focus description, enabling the AI to validate or refine the keyword-based classification. Response parsing via parseRouterResponse extracts JSON from potentially verbose AI responses using regex pattern matching, validates enumerated types, normalizes confidence scores to 0-1 range, and provides sensible defaults when parsing fails. The quickClassify function provides a fast fallback performing pure keyword analysis without AI calls, useful for immediate feedback or when API is unavailable, constructing reasoning text from top matched signals. Additional utilities include buildRouterRefinementPrompt enabling reclassification after gathering more conversation context which may reveal the true transformation nature, parseRefinementResponse for processing reclassification decisions, getTransformationEmoji mapping types to visual indicators (🔧 technical, 🏢 organizational, 💼 business, 🔀 hybrid), and getPersonaLabel providing French labels for assigned personas. The SYSTEM_PROMPT_TRANSFORMATION_ROUTER establishes expert context describing indicators for each transformation type and rules for classification including confidence thresholds and hybrid detection logic. This router forms the critical entry point for the P2-05 chat system, determining which specialized persona (technical expert, organizational change expert, or business expert) should conduct the initial conversation and which axis framework to apply.

# Technical Expert Persona with 12-Axis Question Framework

473-line conversational AI system guiding technical transformation data collection through structured questions, examples, and KPI identification across architecture, performance, security, and infrastructure domains

The persona-tech.ts module implements a sophisticated technical expert conversational AI persona designed to guide users through comprehensive technical transformation data collection across 12 structured axes. The persona embodies a senior technical expert with two decades of experience spanning software architecture (monolith, microservices, event-driven, serverless), performance and scalability engineering (SLO/SLA, latency, availability), cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) and DevOps practices (CI/CD, Kubernetes, Docker), application security (OAuth, RBAC, encryption, GDPR/PCI-DSS compliance), software quality assurance (testing, coverage, technical debt, refactoring), and data engineering (databases, APIs, integrations). The SYSTEM_PROMPT_PERSONA_TECH establishes communication guidelines emphasizing professional yet accessible language, open-ended precise questions, concrete illustrative examples, reformulation for comprehension validation, progressive detail guidance, and seven core rules including understanding global context first, limiting to 1-3 questions per turn, adapting technical depth to user vocabulary, proposing expert-sourced examples, identifying and noting technical KPIs, flagging potential risks or constraints, and concluding each axis with synthetic reformulation. The TECHNICAL_AXIS_QUESTIONS data structure provides comprehensive question frameworks for all 12 axes: problematique explores current system limitations and their impacts with examples like response time issues or legacy maintenance difficulties tracking KPIs like P95 latency and error rates; objectifs_kpi targets measurable technical goals and SLO/SLA specifications with examples like sub-500ms response times or 99.99% availability tracking uptime percentages and cost per request; personas_volumes identifies technical users and system load with examples quantifying TPS peaks and database volumes tracking active users and concurrency; fonctionnalites_mvp defines essential technical capabilities with API endpoint examples and ML model integration tracking delivery metrics; contraintes_techniques captures architecture decisions and technology constraints with examples like microservices on Kubernetes or GCP mandates tracking stack compliance; contraintes_organisationnelles documents team structure and development processes with Scrum examples and environment configurations tracking velocity and PR merge times; non_objectifs excludes out-of-scope items like legacy integrations or unsupported browsers; donnees_existantes catalogs data sources, formats, and quality with examples of PostgreSQL databases and S3 files tracking volumes and quality rates; conformite_risque addresses security and compliance requirements with OAuth2 and encryption examples tracking compliance scores and vulnerability detection times; questions_ouvertes captures pending technical decisions like message broker selection; planning_jalonne establishes technical milestones with concrete dates for environment readiness and production deployment tracking milestone adherence and lead times; indicateurs_succes defines technical validation criteria like 80% test coverage and SonarQube A scores tracking quality metrics and deployment times. The buildAxisQuestionPrompt function constructs context-aware prompts incorporating session type, current axis metadata (label and description), completion progress, available questions (opening plus follow-ups), relevant examples, KPI targets, previous user responses for iterative deepening, and five behavioral rules ensuring focused questioning, precision, contextual examples, comprehension confirmation, and metric notation. The buildAxisSummaryPrompt generates structured extraction requests producing JSON with summary text, key facts array, metrics with name/value/target triplets, risks array, open questions array, and completeness confidence score enabling systematic data capture. The buildAxisTransitionPrompt creates natural conversational pivots acknowledging completed axis understanding, smoothly introducing the next topic, and posing opening questions while maintaining encouraging tone. Utility functions support conversation management: getNextTechnicalAxis follows predefined logical ordering starting with problem definition proceeding through objectives, users, features, constraints, organization, exclusions, data, security, open questions, planning, and success criteria; calculateTechnicalProgress distinguishes required axes (10 mandatory) from optional axes (2: organizational constraints and non-objectives) computing percentage completion and required axis fulfillment; isTechnicalCollectionComplete validates all required axes are addressed; buildTechCompletionMessage generates congratulatory summaries with progress visualization and next step suggestions. The buildTechIntroMessage provides structured onboarding explaining the 12 dimensions and initiating conversation with the problematique question establishing clear expectations and collaborative tone. This persona system enables natural yet comprehensive technical requirements gathering through AI-guided conversations that adapt to user expertise levels, provide contextual examples from senior architect experience, identify critical KPIs systematically, and ensure complete coverage of technical transformation dimensions from problem definition through success metrics.

# Comprehensive Transformation Session Service with 40+ CRUD Operations

651-line service layer providing complete database operations for sessions, fields, variables, and messages with pagination, filtering, and progress tracking

The transformation-session.service.ts module provides a comprehensive data access layer implementing over 40 functions managing the complete lifecycle of transformation sessions, their collected field data, extracted variables, and conversation messages. The service organizes into logical sections covering each entity with separate read and write operations plus utilities. Session read operations offer multiple retrieval patterns: getTransformationSessionById for basic session data, getTransformationSessionWithFields/Variables/Messages for single-relation loading ordered chronologically, getTransformationSessionFull for complete session context with all relations, and getTransformationSessions providing paginated filtered lists with search capabilities across title, type filtering (TECHNICAL/ORGANIZATIONAL/BUSINESS/HYBRID), and status filtering (draft/in_progress/completed/archived) returning TransformationSessionListItem records with calculated progress percentages computed by counting completed axes against required axes per transformation type. Session write operations include createTransformationSession initializing with draft status tied to userId and orgId, updateTransformationSession supporting partial updates on title/type/status, updateTransformationSessionStatus for workflow progression, and deleteTransformationSession for cleanup. Progress tracking through getTransformationSessionProgress aggregates completion metrics loading fields for axis counts and variables for KR linkage counts, computing percentComplete via calculateSessionProgress utility comparing completed axes against type-specific requirements. Field operations manage the axis-specific collected responses with read functions getTransformationFieldById, getTransformationFieldsBySession returning chronologically ordered fields, and getTransformationFieldByAxis leveraging unique sessionId_axis constraint for direct axis lookup. Field write operations include createTransformationField, updateTransformationField with partial update support, critical upsertTransformationField enabling update-or-create pattern essential for conversation flows where axis responses may be refined, and deleteTransformationField for corrections. The upsert pattern uses Prisma's where clause on composite unique constraint sessionId_axis with separate create and update branches ensuring atomic operations preventing race conditions during concurrent axis completion. Variable operations handle the extracted measurable indicators with getTransformationVariableById, getTransformationVariablesBySession returning chronological order, and getTransformationVariableByName using sessionId_name unique constraint for lookup. Variable writes include createTransformationVariable automatically initializing valueCurrent with valueT0 establishing baseline tracking, updateTransformationVariable supporting partial updates across all numeric values (valueT0, valueTarget, valueCurrent) plus metadata fields, deleteTransformationVariable for cleanup, and specialized linkVariableToKeyResult/unlinkVariableFromKeyResult functions enabling bidirectional OKR integration where transformation variables become tracked through KeyResult entities. Message operations maintain conversation history with getTransformationMessageById, getTransformationMessagesBySession with optional limit for pagination, and getRecentTransformationMessages retrieving last N messages ordered DESC then reversed to chronological for efficient tail queries. Message writes include createTransformationMessage storing role (user/assistant/system), content text, and metadata JSON for persona tracking and context, plus deleteTransformationMessage and bulk deleteTransformationMessagesBySession for conversation management. Utility functions support authorization and statistics: transformationSessionExists for pre-checks, isTransformationSessionOwner comparing userId for access control, countTransformationSessionsByOrg/User for dashboard metrics, and getCompletedAxes extracting axis list for progress calculations. All functions apply consistent type casting from Prisma's generated types to domain types defined in @/types/transformation, handling JSON metadata fields via Prisma.InputJsonValue for type safety, and use conditional field spreading (...(data.field !== undefined && { field: data.field })) enabling partial updates where only provided properties are modified. # Variable Extraction System with Pattern Matching and AI Prompts

545-line module extracting measurable variables from conversational text using regex patterns and AI, supporting 8 categories with T0/Target values and confidence scoring

The variable-extractor.ts module implements a sophisticated system for extracting measurable variables from conversational text collected during transformation sessions, supporting both rapid pattern-based extraction and comprehensive AI-powered analysis. The SYSTEM_PROMPT_VARIABLE_EXTRACTOR establishes expert context defining measurable variables as quantifiable indicators with numeric values tracking from initial state (T0) to target goal across eight standard categories: performance for latency and response times, quality for test coverage and error rates, adoption for user engagement and active usage, risk for vulnerabilities and incidents, financial for revenues and costs, operational for productivity and cycle times, satisfaction for NPS and CSAT scores, and efficiency for automation and time savings. The prompt specifies five extraction rules: identify explicit numbers and metrics, deduce T0 and target values when possible, assign appropriate categories, score confidence from 0 to 1, and note source text enabling traceability, with guidance to estimate missing values with reduced confidence when only one value is explicit. The VARIABLE_PATTERNS array defines 11 regex-based extraction patterns covering diverse metric types: percentage patterns capturing test coverage and availability rates, taux patterns for generic rate metrics, latency patterns converting seconds to milliseconds, time-to-market for efficiency metrics, NPS and satisfaction scores, financial metrics parsing euro amounts with K/M multipliers (2K€ becomes 2000, 2M€ becomes 2000000), ROI percentages, user volume counts, TPS throughput rates, incident counts with time periods, and target indicator phrases (objectif, cible, viser) flagging goal values. Each pattern includes extractValue function parsing matched text into numeric values with isTarget flag distinguishing current versus goal values, plus category assignment and unit template for consistent formatting. The buildVariableExtractionPrompt function generates comprehensive AI extraction requests providing session type context, current axis label, conversation text for analysis, and optional list of previously extracted variables preventing duplication, requesting JSON responses with variable arrays containing name in snake_case, French description, valueT0 and valueTarget numerics, unit string, category enum, confidence score 0-1, and sourceText for auditability, plus axisCompleted boolean indicating sufficient documentation and suggestedNextQuestions array for clarification needs. The prompt specifies confidence scoring rules: over 0.7 when both values explicit, 0.4-0.6 when estimating one value, under 0.4 for high uncertainty. Complementary buildVariableValidationPrompt enables post-extraction validation checking name relevance, T0-to-target coherence ensuring targets represent improvement, category correctness, confidence accuracy, and description clarity returning validated variables with warnings and suggestions. The buildMissingVariablesSuggestionPrompt analyzes completed sessions against domain-typical variables suggesting 3-5 important missing indicators with estimated T0/Target values and rationale explaining importance. The parseExtractionResponse function extracts JSON from potentially verbose AI responses using regex pattern matching, validates variable array structure, applies normalizeVariable to each entry converting to ExtractedVariableRaw type, filters out invalid entries with missing names or non-numeric values, and returns VariableExtractionResult with valid variables, axis completion status, and next questions. Variable normalization via normalizeVariable converts names to snake_case, clamps confidence to 0-1 range, normalizes categories against valid enum values defaulting to operational, and ensures all required fields have sensible defaults. The normalizeVariableName utility transforms raw names to lowercase, removes accents using Unicode normalization, replaces non-alphanumeric characters with underscores, trims leading/trailing underscores, and limits to 50 characters for database compatibility. The quickExtractVariables function provides non-AI fallback iterating all patterns against input text, extracting values using pattern-specific extractValue functions, generating snake_case names using template replacement, assigning 0.6 default confidence for pattern matches, constructing 20% improvement targets when only current values found, and deduplicating by name selecting highest confidence matches. Domain helper getDomainTypicalVariables returns curated variable lists per transformation type: technical includes latence_p95, disponibilite, couverture_tests, score_qualite, incidents_production, temps_deploiement; organizational includes enps, time_to_market, taux_adoption, turnover, heures_formation, satisfaction_accompagnement; business includes nps, taux_conversion, ca_additionnel, cout_acquisition, taux_retention, panier_moyen; hybrid combines top 2 from each domain for cross-functional transformations. The isVariableCoherent validation ensures logical directionality defining higher-is-better categories where targets should exceed T0 (performance, quality, adoption, satisfaction, efficiency) and lower-is-better categories where targets should be below T0 (risk), allowing bidirectional financial metrics covering both cost reduction and revenue increase scenarios. The calculateVariableProgress utility computes percentage completion from baseline through current value toward target using linear interpolation clamped to 0-100 range handling edge cases where target equals T0. This comprehensive extraction system enables P2-05e streaming chat to automatically identify trackable metrics from user responses, populate TransformationVariable records with T0/Target pairs, suggest missing critical indicators, validate coherence, and ultimately generate KeyResult entities linking conversation-extracted variables to formal OKR structures.

State management must track messages array accumulating conversation history, loading boolean indicating active streaming, error state capturing failure conditions, and variables array collecting extracted TransformationVariable records as the AI identifies measurable indicators during conversation. Reconnection handling ensures resilience against network interruptions automatically retrying dropped connections with progressive delays preventing server overload. Error management must distinguish network failures, API errors, stream interruptions, and parsing failures providing appropriate user feedback and recovery options. This hook forms the critical React integration layer connecting UI components to the streaming chat backend, enabling real-time conversational experiences where users see AI responses appearing progressively, extracted variables materializing during conversation, and persona transitions happening seamlessly as the transformation type becomes clear through router classification.

# Task Created for Streaming Chat API Route Implementation

Core API endpoint planned with SSE streaming, persona orchestration, variable extraction, and 10 requests/minute rate limiting

A task has been created with ID 1 to implement the core streaming chat API route at /api/ai/chat forming the backend foundation for P2-05e transformation conversations. The implementation specification defines eight critical requirements. First, the POST handler must implement Zod validation schemas ensuring incoming requests contain valid sessionId references and message content conforming to expected types, returning 400 Bad Request with structured error details when validation fails. Second, Server-Sent Events streaming uses ReadableStream API enabling progressive response transmission where AI-generated text chunks stream to clients as they're produced rather than buffering complete responses, dramatically improving perceived responsiveness during long AI generations. Third, persona selection logic determines which specialized expert conducts the conversation by reading the session's transformation type from the database: TECHNICAL sessions route to persona-tech with 12 technical axes, ORGANIZATIONAL sessions route to persona-orga with 14 organizational change management axes, and BUSINESS sessions route to persona-metier with 14 business/product axes, with HYBRID sessions defaulting to the router's suggested persona based on initial classification confidence. Fourth, the orchestration flow implements a two-stage process where initial messages lacking session type invoke the transformation router via quickClassify for rapid keyword-based classification or buildRouterPrompt for AI-powered deep classification, then subsequent messages delegate to the selected persona using buildTechAxisQuestionPrompt, buildOrgaAxisQuestionPrompt, or buildMetierAxisQuestionPrompt generating context-aware questions based on completed axes, conversation history, and axis metadata. Fifth, variable extraction occurs automatically after each user response invoking buildVariableExtractionPrompt with the conversation text, current axis context, and previously extracted variables, parsing responses via parseExtractionResponse to identify new measurable indicators, creating TransformationVariable records through createTransformationVariable service calls, and streaming variable events to clients enabling real-time UI updates as metrics are discovered. Sixth, database persistence calls createTransformationMessage for both user inputs and assistant responses storing role (user/assistant/system), content text, and metadata JSON containing persona identification, covered axes arrays, extracted variable IDs, and confidence scores enabling conversation replay, context reconstruction, and audit trails. Seventh, rate limiting implements the pattern from /api/ai/suggest using in-memory Map tracking request counts per IP address with 60-second sliding windows enforcing maximum 10 requests per minute, returning 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded with retry-after headers, balancing abuse prevention against natural conversation flow where users may send multiple clarifying messages in quick succession. Eighth, error handling must distinguish transformation router failures defaulting to TECHNICAL type for graceful degradation, persona prompt generation failures providing fallback generic prompts, Gemini API errors returning 503 Service Unavailable, database write failures logging errors but continuing stream, variable extraction failures logging but not interrupting conversation flow, and stream interruptions cleaning up resources properly. This API route orchestrates the entire P2-05 conversation system coordinating router classification, persona-driven questioning, variable extraction, message persistence, and real-time streaming into a cohesive user experience where conversations feel natural while systematically collecting structured transformation data.

# Next.js Streaming API Documentation Retrieved from Context7

Five code examples demonstrating ReadableStream and SSE implementation patterns for App Router and Pages Router with Web API abstractions

Context7 documentation query returned five comprehensive examples demonstrating Next.js streaming patterns applicable to the P2-05e chat API implementation. The first example shows custom streaming using Web APIs directly through an iteratorToStream utility function that converts async generators into ReadableStream instances by implementing the pull controller pattern: the async pull(controller) method calls iterator.next() to retrieve { value, done } tuples, enqueuing values via controller.enqueue(value) when data is available or closing the stream via controller.close() when iteration completes, with a makeIterator async generator demonstrating HTML chunk streaming using TextEncoder to convert strings to Uint8Array buffers with 200ms sleep delays between chunks, ultimately returning new Response(stream) to send the readable stream as the HTTP response. The second example demonstrates Pages Router SSE implementation using res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' }) to configure Server-Sent Events headers, then writing chunks in SSE format via res.write(`data: ${i}\n\n`) with proper double newline terminators, iterating 10 times with 1-second delays before calling res.end() to close the connection, showing the lower-level Node.js response API approach available in Pages Router but not App Router. The third example reiterates the App Router ReadableStream pattern providing GET /api/route endpoint documentation explaining the stream generates HTML chunks with delays, highlighting that this approach provides low-level control over stream generation useful for custom scenarios beyond LLM responses. The fourth example demonstrates AI SDK integration using streamText from the ai package with @ai-sdk/openai provider, showing how POST handlers can receive messages arrays, pass them to streamText with model configuration, and return StreamingTextResponse wrapping result.toAIStream() for simplified LLM streaming without manual ReadableStream management. The fifth snippet provides conceptual overview explaining Next.js offers both high-level abstractions via AI SDK for common streaming scenarios and direct Web API access for custom control, with the Web API approach requiring manual async iterator to ReadableStream conversion controlling chunk enqueuing and stream closure timing. These patterns directly inform P2-05e implementation strategy: the chat endpoint should adopt the App Router ReadableStream pattern creating an async generator yielding ChatStreamEvent JSON objects encoded as text chunks (data: {JSON}\n\n) in SSE format, using iteratorToStream or inline pull controller to convert the generator to ReadableStream, returning new Response(stream, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'Connection': 'keep-alive' } }) to establish SSE connection, with the generator orchestrating persona question generation, Gemini streaming consumption via generateContentStream, variable extraction, and database persistence yielding appropriate event types (text/metadata/variable/complete/error) as conversation progresses.

# Comprehensive Transformation Validation Schemas with Chat Request Support

198-line Zod validation file defining schemas for sessions, fields, variables, messages, filters, and chat requests with French error messages

The transformation.ts validation file provides comprehensive Zod schemas for all transformation domain entities with French-language error messages ensuring type-safe data validation across the P2-05 system. The file begins by importing core enums from @/types/transformation and creating corresponding Zod enum schemas: transformationTypeSchema validating TECHNICAL/ORGANIZATIONAL/BUSINESS/HYBRID types, transformationSessionStatusSchema validating draft/in_progress/completed/archived statuses, chatRoleSchema validating user/assistant/system roles, and variableCategorySchema validating the eight metric categories (performance, quality, adoption, risk, financial, operational, satisfaction, efficiency). A reusable uuidSchema validates UUID format with French error message "ID invalide" used throughout for foreign key references. Session schemas include createTransformationSessionSchema requiring title between 3-200 characters and type enum with optional initialDescription limited to 2000 characters enabling router classification from initial user input, and updateTransformationSessionSchema allowing partial updates with all fields optional supporting status transitions and title refinements. Field schemas provide createTransformationFieldSchema validating sessionId UUID, axis name 1-100 characters, required value string, and optional metadata record for extensibility, plus updateTransformationFieldSchema with optional value and metadata enabling axis response refinements. Variable schemas define createTransformationVariableSchema requiring sessionId UUID, name 2-100 characters for snake_case identifiers, numeric valueT0 and valueTarget for baseline and goal tracking, with optional description up to 500 characters, category enum, and unit string up to 50 characters, while updateTransformationVariableSchema allows partial updates including nullable category and unit plus valueCurrent for progress tracking and keyResultId for OKR linking. Message schemas specify createTransformationMessageSchema validating sessionId, role enum discriminating user/assistant/system messages, content between 1-10000 characters accommodating long AI responses, and optional metadata record storing persona identification, covered axes, and extracted variable references. The critical chatRequestSchema validates streaming chat API requests requiring sessionId UUID for conversation context and message content 1-5000 characters with French error "Le message est requis" and "Le message ne peut pas dépasser 5000 caractères" providing clear user feedback on validation failures. Filter schemas include transformationSessionFiltersSchema supporting status and type as either single values or arrays enabling multi-select filtering plus optional search string for title matching, and paginationSchema using z.coerce converting query string numbers to integers with positive constraint, defaulting page to 1 and limit to 20 with maximum limit of 100 preventing resource exhaustion. Type exports use z.infer deriving TypeScript types from schemas ensuring consistency between validation and type definitions: CreateTransformationSessionInput, UpdateTransformationSessionInput, CreateTransformationFieldInput, UpdateTransformationFieldInput, CreateTransformationVariableInput, UpdateTransformationVariableInput, CreateTransformationMessageInput, TransformationSessionFiltersInput, and ChatRequestInput all exported for use in service layer and API routes. This validation infrastructure enables the P2-05e streaming chat API to validate incoming requests via chatRequestSchema.safeParse returning detailed French error messages when validation fails, parse sessionId for database lookups, enforce message length constraints preventing abuse, and maintain type safety throughout the request processing pipeline from API handler through service layer to database operations.

# AI Suggestion Dialog Component with Multi-Type Suggestion Support

React dialog component handles text suggestions and Key Result generation with copy, apply, add, and regenerate actions

The ai-suggestion-dialog.tsx component implements a comprehensive dialog interface for displaying and managing AI-generated suggestions in the OKR platform. The component handles two distinct suggestion modes with intelligent rendering: text suggestions display a single improved string with typing animation and copy-to-clipboard functionality, while Key Result suggestions present an array of structured metric proposals with individual add buttons. The dialog accepts 10 props enabling flexible configuration: open/onOpenChange control visibility, title/description customize header text, isLoading/error manage loading and error states, suggestion/suggestedKeyResults provide the AI outputs, and three callback props (onApplySuggestion, onAddKeyResult, onRegenerate) enable parent component interaction. The component implements five visual states with appropriate UI: loading state shows AiLoadingIndicator with "Génération des suggestions..." message, error state displays red-bordered alert box with AlertCircle icon and error message, text suggestion state renders AiBadge plus suggestion text with AiTypingAnimation for smooth character-by-character reveal plus copy button that updates to checkmark for 2 seconds, Key Results state shows count badge and list of SuggestedKeyResultCard components, and empty state displays centered Sparkles icon with prompt to regenerate. The SuggestedKeyResultCard sub-component provides rich Key Result visualization with title, optional description, metric type badge with French labels (Pourcentage/Nombre/Montant/Oui/Non), start value and target value badges with distinct styling (target uses primary color), optional justification with lightbulb emoji prefix, and add button that transforms to green checkmark "Ajouté" state after clicking. State management uses two React hooks: copiedText boolean tracks clipboard copy with 2-second auto-reset for visual feedback, and addedKRs Set tracks added Key Results by array index preventing duplicate additions. Dialog footer provides three action buttons: Fermer (outline variant with X icon) closes dialog, Régénérer (outline variant with RefreshCw icon that spins during loading) calls onRegenerate callback if provided, and Appliquer (primary variant with Check icon) calls onApplySuggestion for text suggestions. Component integrates shadcn/ui components (Dialog, ScrollArea, Button) and uses lucide-react icons throughout, with toast notifications from sonner for user feedback on copy and add actions.
